### E3 (2026-05-13 micro, same day as E2)

**E3 (2026-05-13 micro, same day as E2):** Git-deploy wiring shipped — direct-upload pattern retired. New GitHub repo `alisendjsc-crypto/wuld-ink` (public) created and seeded with project state. Initial commit `6bc8930` amended to `0ac009a` to use the GitHub noreply email `263501734+alisendjsc-crypto@users.noreply.github.com` (satisfies GitHub's GH007 email-privacy push block). Cloudflare Pages project deleted (direct-upload only; Cloudflare doesn't allow converting direct-upload → Git-connected in-place — confirmed by inspecting every Settings + Deployments page) and recreated as Git-connected via the dedicated `/workers-and-pages/create/pages` URL. **Meaningful gotcha worth flagging for future Cowork sessions:** the unified `/workers-and-pages/create` flow ONLY creates Workers projects (with `npx wrangler deploy` deploy command), NOT Pages projects with the static-site build config Pages users actually want. The dedicated `/workers-and-pages/create/pages` URL routes to the proper 3-step Pages wizard (Select repository → Set up builds and deployments → Deploy site). Project name `wuld-ink` reused (Cloudflare reclaims same-name pages.dev hostname). Build config: framework preset None, build command empty, build output directory `src`, root directory blank, no env vars. First Git deploy from commit `0ac009a` succeeded; reclaimed `wuld-ink.pages.dev`. Custom domains wuld.ink + www.wuld.ink re-attached via Custom domains tab → Set up a custom domain; both initially showed "Verifying" + "Complete DNS setup" link; one click on "Check DNS records" each flipped both to Active with SSL enabled. ~10 min downtime in the detach-to-reattach gap (acceptable per the explicit consent gathered at session start). Sentinel empty commit `c239c9c` (`git commit --allow-empty`) pushed to main → Cloudflare webhook detected within seconds → auto-built and deployed to `4eede190.wuld-ink.pages.dev` → "Automatic deployments enabled" indicator confirmed. End-to-end git push → Pages auto-deploy wiring functional. Future deploys ship by `git push origin main` — no dashboard drag-drop ever again. **Five OneDrive/PowerShell-5.1/encoding/native-stderr issues hit during bootstrap script iteration:** (1) Cowork bash sandbox can't unlink files in OneDrive-synced workspace folder (write-once mount limitation); OneDrive sync also corrupted `.git/config` with 54 NULL bytes during sandbox-side `git init`. Pivoted to PowerShell script for user-side execution. (2) Initial PS script used here-string `@"..."@` for commit message — UTF-8 BOM stripping during Edit operations broke PS 5.1 parser. Rewrote ASCII-only with multi `-m` flag commit. (3) `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` combined with `2>&1` on native git commands treats stderr (e.g., `fatal: not a git repository` probes) as terminating errors; removed Stop mode + check `$LASTEXITCODE` manually. (4) GitHub blocked initial push (GH007) due to commit author using user's primary private email; resolved via `git config user.email` to noreply + `git commit --amend --reset-author --no-edit` + re-push. (5) Coordinate clicking unreliable for "Connect GitHub" tile on unified create flow; switched to `find` + ref_id clicks. **Bootstrap artifact `setup-git.ps1` shipped in the repo at root** (idempotent one-shot init+commit handling all of the above failure modes; ASCII-only, no `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, `cmd /c rd /s /q` fallback for OneDrive lock cases, attribute-clearing pass before rm). Harmless if it stays — documents the bootstrap process. Removable in a future commit if desired. **Chrome MCP usage retrospective:** ~60-70 Chrome calls across E3 — repo creation (~8), Pages config (~20: includes the wasted Workers flow detour), domain detach/reattach (~15), sentinel deploy verification (~5), Cloudflare dashboard nav latency (~15). Workers vs. Pages flow detour cost ~6-8 unnecessary calls; future Pages-project create sessions should go directly to `/workers-and-pages/create/pages`. The synthetic-file-upload limitation from E2 didn't bite this session because Git-deploy bypasses file uploads entirely.

## Session-D era (Void Engine misread)

### Misread log (session D, 2026-05-13)

- **What I read:** "Void Engine — prompt tool, with Signal and Transmission components" (`docs/wuld-ink-cowork-brief.md` line 64).
- **How I parsed it:** "prompt tool" = tool that *operates on* prompts (text-in, text-out, transformation-style instrument).
- **Actual meaning:** "prompt tool" = tool that *builds* prompts (the suite's AI image-prompt builder).
- **The clarifying questions I did ask at D start were UI-shape questions** (single textarea vs. structured form, output position, registry vs. pipeline). They locked the surface details of the wrong artifact.
- **The clarifying question I did NOT ask:** *Does `/void-engine/` host an existing suite app, or is this its own new thing?* That was the architectural-origin question. Asking it would have surfaced the suite immediately and prevented the misread.
- **Failure mode to log permanently:** when a project surface shares a name with an external artifact (suite engine, library substrate, anything cross-project), ASK about origin before building. Don't infer from naming alone.

### Direction locked (rebuild fork chosen 2026-05-13)

- `wuld.ink/void-engine/` will be a faithful public **port of the suite Void Engine** (image-prompt builder, ~190 modifier entries across 12 categories, positive/negative prompt compiler, presets, chaos roll, deep scan, diagnosis modal, corpus analyzer, session archive via `localStorage`). Suite-Claude maintains the canonical source; wuld.ink-side hosts the public port.
- **Naming collision resolves cleanly under this fork:** there is ONE Void Engine. Same artifact, suite is the source-of-truth, wuld.ink is the public face.
- **Logic preservation principle for the port:** suite's JS is the canonical source. Port should preserve it as-is to the maximum extent compatible with the wuld.ink chrome. Don't re-implement what the suite has already hardened across multiple versions.
- **Styling reconciliation is the bounded transformation:** suite's CSS gets replaced with wuld.ink design tokens (`var(--c-bg)`, `var(--c-accent)`, `var(--font-mono)`, etc.); suite's JS stays untouched. Layout grammar may need reconciliation depending on suite's current shape — pending suite-Claude's next-round file export.

### What session D' will roll back

- `src/components/void-engine.css` (~8.3 KB) — text-transformer styling. Delete; not reusable for image-prompt builder layout.
- `src/components/void-engine.js` (~9.2 KB) — registry + PRNG + DOM controller for text transforms. Delete; suite app has its own controller, no port value.
- `src/void-engine/index.html` — full overwrite with suite Void Engine port wrapped in wuld.ink chrome (site header / nav / footer / page hero).
- Homepage Void card already rolled back to `data-status="forthcoming"` this turn (tag updated to "Image-prompt builder — port pending"); no further index.html change needed for the rollback step itself.

## Standalone session deliverables blocks (pre-K)

### Session D deliverables (2026-05-13)

- **`src/components/void-engine.css`** (~8.3 KB) — instrument styling: signal textarea (blood-red accent rail, mono, brutalist border, dim italic placeholder, focus-visible ring), mode radiogroup (button row with hairline borders between presets, active mode flips to accent fill), seed input (labeled tag + numeric field, "auto" placeholder when empty), transmit button (right-aligned via margin-inline-start: auto on desktop, full-width on mobile), section-rule with absolutely-positioned "TRANSMISSION" label punching through, transmission output region (accent-dim rail goes hot when transmitted), meta readout (preset · seed · char count), full mobile fallback (stacks vertically <640px), screen-reader-only utility class.
- **`src/components/void-engine.js`** (~9.2 KB) — IIFE-scoped controller. Mulberry32 seeded PRNG; xmur3 string-to-seed hash for empty-seed-input fallthrough (auto-seed becomes pure function of Signal content → reproducible without manual seed entry). Registry as Map: `register(slug, {label, transform})`. Two stubs auto-registered on boot: `null` (passthrough) and `inversion` (Array.from + reverse + join — surrogate-pair safe). Public API exposed at `window.VoidEngine` with `register`, `list`, `run`, `rehydrate`. DOM hydration: builds radio buttons from registry, wires keyboard arrow nav within radiogroup, form submit handler, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter shortcut from textarea, empty-signal handling falls back to idle state, error state on transform throw. Try/catch around `mod.transform()` so a buggy chat-authored preset can't take down the page.
- **`src/void-engine/index.html`** — placeholder `[ · ]` frame replaced with the live instrument. Page-intro paragraph in italic serif body register sets the instrument's mood without philosophical content. Inline `<script>` chat-side authoring contract documented in a trailing comment block — example registration pattern + reminder to call `VoidEngine.rehydrate()` after appending presets.
- **`src/index.html`** — homepage Void card `data-status="forthcoming"` attribute removed; card is now live-state (no `↳` prefix on the tag).

**Smoke-test results:** 6/6 PRNG + registry unit tests pass (passthrough, inversion, surrogate-pair safe inversion, content-deterministic auto-seed, explicit seed honored, PRNG same-seed reproducibility). Live HTTP server probe: void-engine page returns 200 (5128 bytes), all 6 referenced assets resolve 200, all expected structural elements present (void-engine section, signal input, modes radiogroup, transmission output, aria-live polite, void-engine.js script tag, role="radiogroup"). JS passes `node -c` syntax check. CSS braces balanced (39 open / 39 close). Note: bash mount of `index.html` shows a stale pre-session-B snapshot (mtime 00:56) so the homepage edit isn't visible to bash but IS visible to the file-tool Read — the workspace folder (which Cloudflare Pages deploys from) reflects the live edit.

**Chat-side authoring contract for Void Engine transmission modes:** SUPERSEDED by D'. The text-transformer registry contract no longer exists. - **Cover-axis fix (session-start aesthetic note from Josiah).** Screenshot showed the W.U.L.D. INCORPORATED video sitting visibly right-of-axis within its bracketed frame; subhead `WORTHLESS · USELESS · LIFELESS · DEAD` + INDEX↓ rendered correctly on page axis, confirming the bug was local to the cover-mark video element. Diagnosis: `.cover-mark--video` is an h1 with `display:flex; width:100%; max-width:50rem;` but **no `margin-inline:auto`**. Block-level h1 doesn't honor parent's `text-align:center` for its own box positioning when capped under parent width — it defaults to the start edge. Parent `.cover-mark-block` is wider than 50rem (capped at `--w-max`), so the h1 sat left-of-center within it. Flex `justify-content:center` correctly centered brackets+video INSIDE the h1, but the h1 itself was offset. Subhead + INDEX↓ rendered correctly because they're text within text-align:center'd block-flow (not flex containers). Fix: one-line `margin-inline: auto` addition to `.cover-mark--video` rules, with inline comment explaining the axis-fix rationale for future debug-readers. **Post-deploy patch (same day, post-session-J commit):** structural centering shipped clean (curl-verified 5/5 `margin-inline:auto` rules in deployed HTML; pre-J figure-shifted-right is now figure-centered). Initial follow-on tune shipped + reverted: max-width 50rem → 32rem → 50rem. Josiah preferred the original frame size; the bracket-hug-the-figure problem turned out to be a misread of the actual visual issue — the real misalignment was the cover SUBHEAD (`Worthless · Useless · Lifeless · Dead`), not the video frame. **Subhead root cause logged:** `base.css` applies `max-width: var(--w-prose)` to ALL `<p>` elements as a global prose-readability default. The subhead is a `<p>`, so its box was capped at prose-width (~65ch) — but without `margin-inline:auto`, the constrained box sat at the start edge of `.cover-mark-block` (block elements default to start, not center). `text-align:center` centered the text within the narrow left-edge box, NOT within the full parent. The slab rule (`<hr>`) and INDEX↓ (`<p>` with its own `margin-inline:auto`) didn't have this issue. Fix: one-line `margin-inline: auto` on `.cover-subhead` with inline comment explaining the base.css interaction. **Lesson logged for future Cowork:** when a global rule in `base.css` constrains an element type's box (max-width, max-content, etc.), per-component CSS for that element type must add `margin-inline:auto` to center the constrained box — text-align:center alone only centers content WITHIN the box, not the box within its parent. Audit existing `<p>` instances on the homepage for similar latent issues (cover-descent has its own margin-inline:auto from session G fix, so it's already safe).

- **Footer propagation to 13 shells via shared component CSS.** Promoted homepage `.home-footer` rules to NEW `/components/footer.css` (~60 lines, single canonical source for `.page-footer` + `.page-footer-inner` + `.copyright strong` + `.disclaimer-pending` + `.disclaimer-pending::before`). Canonical class is `.page-footer` (renamed from `.home-footer` on homepage + from `.site-footer` on templates/essay.html). Per session-I lesson 3: component CSS earns its keep on the second use — at 13 surfaces wanting the same pattern, promotion is amply justified. All 13 shells now consume the shared stylesheet via `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/components/footer.css">` in head, with the canonical body pattern (`<span class="copyright">` + `<span class="disclaimer-pending">`).

  - **13-file roster:** 9 page-footer shells (`index.html` home + `essays/index` + `essays/sanguinolentum-vestigium` + `argument-library` + `book` + `blog` + `glossary/index` + `watch` + `void-engine` [special, see below]), 1 site-footer template (`templates/essay`), 3 glossary files with NO previous footer (`glossary/_template` + `glossary/alogical-isness` + `glossary/contextus-claudit` — footer ADDED between `</main>` and script tags). Scaffold-era footer text (`WULD · wuld.ink · 2026–` + `Cloudflare Pages + R2`) gone from every file. Smoke-checked via grep: 0 occurrences of scaffold text, 31 occurrences of canonical `copyright|disclaimer-pending` across 13 expected files.
  - **Void-engine special case (D'' triptych chrome).** Footer keeps its inline-styled chrome (`#030303` bg, `#8a847b` text, `#2a2a2a` border, centered single-line text) per session-D'' chrome-wrap discipline — blends with canonical triptych register, NOT umbrella tokens. Linking footer.css there would have been a no-op visually (inline-style specificity wins) AND introduced subtle conflict risk with the canonical inline `<style>` block. Decision: SKIP footer.css link to void-engine, just update the footer body text to: `© Josiah S. Cooper · 2010–2026 · all rights reserved · return to index`. The disclaimer-pending pointer is umbrella-only register (not instrument-mode-fit); return-to-index affordance preserved as the meaningful umbrella signpost in the triptych context.
  - **Watch one-off.** Footer had a `<span><a href="/" ...>← Return to index</a></span>` second span instead of the scaffold `Cloudflare Pages + R2` (different pattern variant from session G). Replaced with the canonical copyright + disclaimer pattern; return-to-index removed (site-header logo already provides homepage navigation; redundant in footer).
  - **Templates/essay.html (`.site-footer` third class-name variant).** Renamed `.site-footer` → `.page-footer` in HTML body, removed inline `.site-footer*` rule block, added footer.css link. Now consistent with canonical pattern.
  - **Deferred cleanup.** Inline `.page-footer*` rule blocks still live in the 8 standard shells' `<style>` tags as dead code (~20 lines × 8 = ~160 lines total). Linked footer.css comes after the inline rules in head source order, so the linked stylesheet wins; the inline rules are dead but harmless. Removable in a future micro-session via parallel Edits; not blocking.

**Files touched (session J):** `src/components/footer.css` (NEW, ~60 lines), `src/index.html` (cover-axis fix + footer.css link + dead-rule removal + class rename in HTML + Malgré Tout 09th grid card), 9 page-shell HTML files (footer.css link + footer body rewrite), `src/templates/essay.html` (link + inline-rule removal + class rename + body rewrite), 3 glossary files (link + footer HTML insert between main + scripts), 1 void-engine (footer body text only — skipped link). **15 files modified + 1 new = 16 total.** Same-day commit waves expected: deliverables first (16 files), docs second (CLAUDE.md + memory).

**Tool-budget retrospective (session J):** Projected 30-50 at session start with relay-doc-as-light triage; actual ~55 by close. Slightly over projection — the watch one-off (different pattern variant required separate Edit), the void-engine special-case handling, and the cover-axis mid-session aesthetic interrupt added ~5 unplanned calls. Within ceiling. Pre-flag discipline held: warned at session start about footer propagation being the bulk-spend item; that bore out (footer propagation accounted for ~30 calls of the total).

**Lessons logged for future Cowork sessions:**
1. **Mid-session screenshots from Josiah → triage immediately, fix inline if fast.** The cover-axis fix was a one-line CSS edit shippable in the same turn as the message; deferring it would have created context-switching overhead and risked forgetting. The system-reminder pattern enforces this discipline ("you MUST address the user's message").
2. **Grep output escaping is not byte-faithful to the file.** Watch's footer had `href="/"` in the actual file but grep rendered it as `href="\"` (backslash escape). Copy-pasting grep output into Edit's `old_string` failed string-match. Always Read the file directly when Edit string-match fails — grep is for locating, not for copy-pasting source bytes.
3. **Dead CSS accumulation is acceptable short-term debt when promoting to component.** Removing inline duplicates costs N edits per file (where N = shells); leaving them as dead code (~160 lines total across 8 files) costs zero visual impact + buys ~8 edits worth of tool budget. The right move when budget pressure is real and visual outcomes match between source-order-wins-anyway alternatives. Sweep can be its own micro-session.
4. **When a shared component diverges by design on one surface (like void-engine's triptych chrome), don't extend the component there.** Linking the shared stylesheet to a surface that overrides everything inline is cognitive noise + carries subtle conflict risk. Component CSS is for surfaces that share register; surfaces that diverge by design get treated as their own case.
5. **Label-picking for new homepage grid cards.** Six register-tight options considered for the 09th card: "Treatise" (chosen — philosophical weight, distinguishes from "Long-work"), "Volume" (too neutral), "Standalone" (relation-descriptor, weaker than category), "Published" (plain), "Manifeste" (matches French title but obscures the umbrella's English-default chrome), "Tome" (pretentious-without-payoff). Pattern: pick the label that descripts CATEGORY/MODE (like "Long-form" / "Reference" / "Vocabulary") not the artifact-name or relation-to-other-works.

(xiii) **Coincidence of byte-count match between two different corruption states is real-world** — upload (clean + null padding = 72509 B) and on-disk (clean + truncated content = 72509 B) hit same total by accident. `diff` flagged "Binary files differ" but `wc -lc` showed same line counts because both files ended without trailing newline at same byte position. Discipline: when file mtime + byte count look matching but content audit needed, use `cat -A | tail` to detect null-byte tails + `diff` (which uses content-comparison) to detect substantive differences. md5 catches most cases; `diff` catches the rest.

(xvii) **HC mode distinction is a stroke-weight problem not a color problem when color tokens are already at AAA extremes.** Pattern: when an accessibility-mode cascade only varies colors but inherits stroke/weight/spacing tokens from `:root`, the visual delta is bounded by what color can do — and at AAA extremes (`#000`/`#fff`/lifted accent/yellow focus) color can't do much beyond what's already on the page. Escalation paths from there in priority order: (a) border-width tokens — most impact, propagates to chrome separators globally; (b) font-weight tokens — depends on font-family weight availability (EB Garamond 400→600 gap, no 500 weight loaded); (c) spacing tokens — risky, can reflow layout; (d) outline-offset — narrow visibility win on focus only. Decision tree for future chrome instruments (e.g., line-height slider, font-family override, color-blind palette picker): (1) shared visual register + render-adjacency with existing instruments → append to `mode-toggle.{css,js}`; (2) independent visual register OR different render-zone → new component files. Threshold judgment per-instrument; promote-to-`/components/chrome.css` if 3+ chrome-instrument components share same files. (xix) **HC verify-first approach paid off** — AskUserQuestion option `Verify toggle first, then escalate` triggered reading mode-toggle.js + cross-referencing token values BEFORE recoloring. Surface read confirmed toggle worked + colors already at extremes → escalation in correct direction (strokes not colors). Had we picked `Full rebuild assuming colors-are-close`, would have shipped a recolor that wouldn't have moved the needle + cost ~15 extra calls of mis-direction. Pattern: when user describes mode as "reads too close" to another mode, FIRST verify the toggle mechanism actually fires + SECOND audit which tokens vary vs which inherit — escalation target follows from where the inheritance gap is, not from where the visual closeness reads.

The `-NoNewline` flag controls trailing newline only; the `UTF8` encoding (in PS 5.x; renamed `UTF8NoBOM` in PS 6+) always emits the 3-byte BOM (`EF BB BF`). Pages `_redirects` parser silently rejected the BOM-prefixed rule. Workaround: `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($path, [System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($content))` for pure-ASCII content (bulletproof). For UTF-8-required content, `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $content, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))` is K15-canonical but verify BOM via xxd post-write. Lock: any file destined for parsers that reject BOM gets xxd-verification post-write before push. (xxv) **Cloudflare Pages "Pretty URLs" interacts with `_redirects` 200-rewrites by extension-stripping the target**: rule `/  /combined.html  200` rewrites `/` to `/combined.html` internally, then Pretty URLs 308s `/combined.html` → `/combined` externally, producing a visible redirect chain. Fix: target the extension-stripped form `/combined` directly. The `.html` form is INVALID as a rewrite target on a Pages project with Pretty URLs enabled. (xxvi) **`gh` CLI absent in default PS environment**; publication script has gh-fallback that prints description string for manual paste. Operator-side install (winget/scoop/chocolatey) would automate the description-update path but is non-blocking. (xxvii) **PS script step 11 identity-set failure mode**: freshly-cloned repo has no local `user.email`/`user.name`; global config is unset; commit refuses with "Author identity unknown". Future revision of `publish-library-*.ps1` should set local identity post-clone (between step 5 and 6): `git -C $REPO_LOCAL config user.email $WULDINK_EMAIL; git -C $REPO_LOCAL config user.name $WULDINK_NAME` with constants at script top. Carry-forward to K24f. (xxviii) **Cloudflare Workers vs Pages create-flow ambiguity**: in the merged Workers-and-Pages dashboard, the default "Connect to Git" flow creates a Workers project. The "Pages" tab is rendered in tiny secondary text (per operator feedback) and easy to miss. Workers projects require wrangler.toml or fail with `Could not detect a directory containing static files`. Lock for future similar work: explicitly verify the project type tab BEFORE clicking through. (xxix) **Pages root URL fallback behavior**: Pages serves `index.html` at `/` by default; if absent, returns 404. `_redirects` 200-rewrite is the correct fix for single-file repos where the filename is md5-binding (preserves canonical filename + serves at root); `index.html` shim or `combined.html` rename are inferior (filename-collision or filename-divergence). (xxx) **Deploy-critical chain has natural operator-side break points** (PS script execution, GitHub web UI for description, Cloudflare Pages create, Cloudflare custom domain attach). Cowork pattern at each break: emit instructions precisely + accept report-back + run single-bash-call verification before continuing. (lii) **K24g lesson xxxvi pre-emptive mitigation works cleanly** - since K24j bulk-inject touched disclaimers (workstream 2), the Sec.07 edit (workstream 3) was authored as a `git show HEAD:path | python str.replace + bulk-inject re-application + atomic write` pipeline in one bash call. K24f lesson xxxi pattern (question count scales with unresolved decision axes after diagnostic) reaches its limit case at 0 questions when the user has already pre-resolved all axes. (liv) **YouTube IFrame API `setShuffle(true)` operates on YT-internal playlist order**, not externally-stable shuffle indices. Cross-page resume relies on `currentVideoId` (stable video ID) + `lastPositionSec` (stable position), NOT shuffle index (page-local). Effect: when user navigates from page A to page B, the *same video* resumes at the *same position*, but the *next track in shuffle order* may differ from what page A's shuffle would have queued next. This is acceptable for ambient register (the resume is the load-bearing UX promise; "what's next" is implicitly random anyway under shuffle). Documented in JS comments. (lv) **Existing-file content derivation from `git show HEAD:path` via `subprocess.check_output`** is the durable K24g lesson xxxvi mitigation for sandbox-read truncation. Pattern: `data = subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"HEAD:{path}"])` -> apply all session edits in-memory -> single atomic `open(path, "wb").write(data)`. Reusable for any multi-edit-same-file workstream pattern.

Lock pattern for any future per-video logic over a YT playlist (per-track skip-UI, custom advance behavior, end-of-track analytics): polling > event-driven. Same polling loop serves multiple consumers (slider position + time readout + loop-one detection) at single setInterval cost. Reusable for any future progress-slider, scrub-bar, or auto-updating numeric control. (cvii) **Component-name-conflict — ALWAYS git-log existing components before authoring fresh.** K28 authored fresh `theater-mode.css|js` without checking `git log src/components/theater-mode.*` first; overwrote K24k pre-existing component (commit `1715a42`) that already coordinates with ambient-player via custom events + is wired into archive/music pages. Lock: BEFORE writing any new file under `src/components/`, run `git log --oneline -- src/components/<name>.*` AND `test -f src/components/<name>.*` to confirm absence. Same applies to any commonly-named path (any `index.html` under a new dir, any obvious component name). The trigger is: "I'm about to author a component with a plausibly-already-existing name." If the test is even ambiguous, check git. K28 cost: ~5 calls overhead + adapted recommendations markup to existing contract.

(cviii) **Em-dash literal vs entity mismatch in byte-pattern replacement.** Atomic Python byte-level `disk.replace(OLD, NEW)` operations require OLD to match EXACTLY what's on disk. K28 OLD pattern used `&mdash;` HTML entity but disk had raw UTF-8 em-dash `\xe2\x80\x94`. AssertionError on `assert OLD in disk`. Diagnose pre-build: `grep -aP "\xe2\x80\x94" <file>` (raw byte sequence) vs `grep "&mdash;" <file>` (entity). Pattern: ALWAYS verify on-disk form via grep before crafting OLD pattern for any HTML file with em-dashes / en-dashes / curly-quotes / non-ASCII glyphs. K28 hit this on recommendations featured-button replace; recovery rewrote OLD with raw UTF-8 em-dash via Write tool then re-read as bytes (write-to-file + read-as-bytes pattern from K28 WS A). Cost: ~1 Python invocation.

EOF`) — atomic write succeeded at 3811 B / 135 lines. New evidence for K22 vii: same-baseline-byte truncation observed in addition to >5KB threshold and Edit-cumulative-growth (K25 xc / K27 ci). **K28b same-session amendment 2 (post-K28a-deploy QA fix — banner positioning):** Operator-side QA on K28a banner showed wrong region of image visible everywhere — homepage missed the W.U.L.D. text, non-home pages showed truncated band without figure presence. Root cause: `object-position: center 78%` (default) and `center 82%` (homepage) were both biased toward bottom but with a too-tight container (5rem / 3.5rem), the visible slice cropped above the actual wordmark band. Wordmark sits at image y=382-425 (87-96% of 443px height); figure silhouette at y=20-180 (5-40%). Pre-fix Python-side wordmark-position audit confirmed coordinates via per-row brightness/red-channel max analysis. **K28b fix:** (i) **Non-home banner returns to figure-focused presentation** at `height: 9rem` (~144px) — between K28's `22vh` and K28a's `5rem`, per operator's "a little less space" instruction. `object-position: center 15%` shows image y range 15-72% (figure region centered). (ii) **Homepage banner shows wordmark only** at `height: 4rem` (~64px). `object-position: center bottom` (100% y) shows image bottom 64px = y range 379-443, capturing the wordmark cleanly. (iii) Mobile breakpoint: non-home `6rem` / home `3rem`. nav.css final 4649 B / md5 `67d12374`. Cache-bump K28a → K28b: 54 files / 423 swaps. **K28b lessons logged:** (cxv) **`object-position` percentage math for `object-fit: cover` requires inverted reasoning relative to natural image coordinates.** With image taller than container in the cover case, percentage value `p%` shows visible slice from image pixel `excess × p/100` to `excess × p/100 + container_height`, where `excess = image_height - container_height`. NOT the image's `p%` point directly. So to show image pixel-y range `Y_start` to `Y_end`, compute `p% = (Y_start / excess) × 100`. K28a's `82%` for a 56px container on 443px image showed pixels `(387) to (443)` which is the wordmark BAND, but at that container size, only 56px of the wordmark + below was visible — and the wordmark "W.U.L.D.: INCORPORATED" rendered too small to be legible. The fix at K28b is `center bottom` (= 100%) + `height: 4rem` (64px) to give the wordmark slightly more vertical room. (cxvi) **Per-row image analysis via NumPy/PIL is the right diagnostic for object-position tuning.** Before guessing CSS percentages, run a Python script that maps the image content rows to y-coordinates (R-channel max per row + brightness per row + per-third aggregate). Locks the CSS-position decision to data instead of trial-and-error. ~5 lines of code; saves N iterations of "deploy + look + revise".

Browsers tolerate mid-document truncation (HTML parsers are lenient; missing close tags auto-closed). Symptom on archive: ambient-player markup is rendered (it sits BEFORE the truncation point) but the script that would activate the player never loads (truncated `<script src=` line never completes parsing) — so ambient-player markup is present in DOM but the player widget never initializes. Symptom on library-about: ambient-player markup itself truncated mid-button; no script tag at all. Lock: ADD `tail -c 50 <file>` + `endswith(b'</html>\n')` check to STANDING discipline at EVERY session-open diagnostic, not just post-Edit. Add to canonical diagnostic-first opening template under "K30 surfaces alive" section. Extends K25 xc + K27 ci + K28 cix + K28a cxiii truncation-detection family: K28a cxiii caught Edit-tool NUL-padding immediately post-edit; K31 cxxviii catches OLDER truncation that survived session close. Recovery: per-file canonical-tail rebuild via cut-and-rebuild (find last verified-clean point, append clean tail). The truncated content itself can usually be reconstructed from a known-canonical sibling page (essays/book/etc. used as ground truth).

(cxxix) **Ambient-player presence bug — script-include-without-markup pattern in K26+ pages.** chat/contact/donations (K26) + recommendations (K26, pre-content-fill at K28 D2) all shipped with `<script src="/components/ambient-player.js?v=...">` includes but no `<div id="ambient-player">` markup block. Implicit-template-omission: the K26 templates that authored these new tabs included the script reference (probably copied from a working sibling) without realizing the script needs the markup hook to find. Script loads silently, finds nothing, no-ops. Bug invisible at console (no error; missing element check returns null safely). Detection vector: site-wide grep for pages with `ambient-player.js` AND without `id="ambient-player"`. Lock pattern: when adding ambient-player.js to a new page during build, ALWAYS pair with the canonical markup block; verify presence via `grep -l 'id="ambient-player"' <new_page>` after authoring. Add `(has_js AND has_markup) OR (has_neither)` audit to nav-hash-style sweep — same shape as K25 xci nav-drift detection but for component dependencies.

(cxxx) **Multimodal Read + Google-AI-overlay screenshots = identification in 1 call per piece.** Operator's 10 art screenshots were captured FROM Google reverse-image-search results pages, with the AI overlay panel visible in-frame. Reading each screenshot via Read tool yielded immediate artist + work + year identification for 7/10 pieces (Sherman #39, Serrano Heaven and Hell, Witkin La Belle et La Bête, Witkin Hooded Woman, Witkin Poet, Sherman #6, Theologian album cover). 3/10 needed minor WebSearch verification (Sherman kitchen-scene-identification to #3, Witkin preparatory study generic identification, Sissisters album cover canonical URL). Cost: 10 Read + 4 WebSearch = 14 identification calls. Counterfactual without AI-overlay-in-screenshot: each piece would need reverse-image-search round-trip (~3-5 calls each = 30-50 total). 50%+ reduction. Pattern: when operator captures screenshots FROM a Google Lens search results page (recognizable by Google logo + "Add to your search" + AI Overview panel), the identification IS already in the screenshot; Read the screenshot first, only WebSearch for verification or canonical-URL hunting. If operator's workflow shifts to raw camera/clipboard captures without search context, this pattern won't apply — and the call cost reverts to reverse-image-search-per-piece.

(cxxxi) **Shared-canonical-URL pattern extends from N=2 to N=3+.** K30 cxxiii locked the pattern at N=2 (NTT + WHABH → same WHABH URL). K31 ships N=3 (Sherman #3 + #6 + #39 all → Wikipedia Untitled Film Stills series article) and N=3 again (Witkin Hooded + Belle + preparatory → Wikipedia Joel-Peter Witkin artist article; #8 Poet has its own Smithsonian URL). Acceptable when (a) no per-work Wikipedia coverage exists AND (b) the shared anchor IS the canonical hub for the series or artist. Card-note text disambiguates between same-URL siblings (year + series-position + visible-content tag). Not acceptable when shared-URL is incidental (e.g., random art-blog with multiple unrelated artists). Lock heuristic: prefer per-work URL > artist URL > series URL > publisher URL > arbitrary-blog URL.

**K32 lessons logged:**

(cxxxix) **K28a cxiii NUL-padding refined: BYTE-SHORTER Edits leave trailing NULs.** Refined trigger: NUL padding occurs ONLY when `new_string` is BYTES-SHORTER than `old_string`; same-length and longer Edits are NUL-safe. Edit tool overwrites in place without disk-truncate when content shrinks. Mitigation: audit `d.count(bytes([0]))` post any Edit where new content might be shorter, and `d.rstrip(bytes([0]))` + atomic rewrite if NULs present.

(cxl) **Read tool path-form requires connected folder.** `/sessions/<UUID>/mnt/outputs/...` rejected by Read with "outside this session\'s connected folders"; same files copied to a connected folder work via Windows-path Read. (cxli) **Prompt-leak detectable across 4 flavor classes — tautological self-reference is the trump card.** Gallery lede contained: (i) meta-shape declarative ("Exhibition handout in the form of a wall"), (ii) my-side typography/voice jargon ("register", "analog-decay"), (iii) prompt-status flavor ("Currently: plates I-XXVII, batches 01-02"), (iv) tautological self-reference ("the wall text refuses the conventions of wall text"). Per operator clarification, (iv) was the actual leak; (i) and (ii) were acceptable descriptive frame in operator\'s voice; (iii) was acceptable factual metadata. Audit pattern: grep `<p class="page-intro">` + meta-description content for tautologies first, then my-side voice-instrument vocabulary. Don\'t pre-empt operator\'s descriptive prose.

(cxlii) **Same-byte-count Edit is NUL-safe (K31c cxxxix complement).** When `new_string` byte-length equals `old_string` byte-length, Edit overwrites in place with NO trailing NULs. Combined with cxxxix: NUL audit needed ONLY when intended Edit shrinks content; same-length and longer Edits skip audit.

(cxliii) **Operator-supplied URLs may include tracking params — strip to canonical clean form.** K31d operator-supplied IMDB URL had tracking params; canonical form matches the other 4 film cards\' shape and avoids referrer-tracking pollution. Lock: when operator pastes URL with query/fragment tracking params, strip to clean form unless the params are functional. Refines K31a cxxxiii: mechanical with typographic + URL-hygiene normalization.

(cxliv) **Operator post-deploy QA + iteration is the right shape for editorial-content placement.** K32 had 2 post-deploy iteration cycles (gallery lede revert+rewrite; archive caption refinements). Pattern: ship scaffold with neutral placeholders + operator-visibility audit on deployed surface + minimal-edit refinement based on operator\'s specific corrections. Reduces wasted authoring effort vs trying to predict operator preferences up front. Particularly effective for editorial-content placement where Cowork mechanical discipline can\'t anticipate operator\'s exact voice or specific factual corrections.

**K35 lessons logged:**

(clvii) **Verify-don't-make-worse semantics > strict-absolute semantics for batch operations on shared codebases.** GUI's initial verify_bytes used absolute checks (`new.endswith(b"</html>\n")`); failed on void-engine pre-existing trailing-newline absence, which blocked the entire 54-file cache-bump despite the operation itself being benign. Refactor to `verify_bytes(rel, new, old=None)` with "regression-only" semantics when old is supplied: NUL/CR/tail bad only if new is WORSE than old. Lock: any verification helper that runs across a multi-file batch must distinguish "regression introduced by this op" from "pre-existing invariant violation"; the former blocks, the latter does not. Refinement of K28a cxiii + K31 cxxviii — those discipline rules locked WHAT to check; cxlvii locks the SEMANTICS of the check when other code might be in non-canonical state. Doesn't replace fix-the-pre-existing-issue effort (void-engine was still fixed inline this session); does mean batch ops are robust against ANY single bad file blocking the batch.

(clviii) **Edit-tool truncation in cumulative-Edit sequences extends to Cowork-authored Python files, not just HTML.** K27 ci originally locked the pattern around HTML edits via `git show HEAD:path` re-derive; K35 reproduced it on `tools/wuld-gui/app.py` after 3 cumulative Edits (verify_bytes refactor: signature change + op_preview update + op_commit update). py_compile catches Python truncations instantly (SyntaxError unclosed paren); HTML truncations are silent-shipping per K31 cxxviii. Lock: ANY multi-Edit-on-same-file pattern triggers K27 ci → atomic Python rewrite from FIRST patch, regardless of file type. The 3rd Edit IS the failure point N=2 confirmation. Recovery cost: ~3-5 calls (find truncation byte / rebuild tail / re-test). Avoided cost if K27 ci is invoked at FIRST patch: ~2 calls saved per file per session.

(clix) **GUI-handout split at 7+7 pattern count maps cleanly to Flask-supportable mechanical vs prose-authoring judgment.** Operator screenshot pre-commit ("GUI handles bottom 60%; handout covers top 40%") was vibe-quantified — actual on-disk pattern audit (WS2) returned 7 GUI + 7 handout patterns (50/50 by count, but mechanical patterns fire ~3-5x more frequently per K22-K34 commit grep, recovering the 60/40 ratio by volume). Lock: the 60/40 split is real and stable; the GUI doesn't need to grow toward handout territory and the handout doesn't need to absorb mechanical operations. Future scope additions land in whichever side fits the operation's judgment requirement, without re-litigating the split. The path-selector table in the handout names which path for which task; expand the table as new patterns surface rather than rewriting either component.

(clx) **Mid-session file-name confusion (uploads/session-K25-prompt.md vs session-K35-prompt.md) cost 1 conversation turn but no actual tool budget.** Operator uploaded wrong prompt file at K35 open (K25 prompt, mis-named); Cowork Read-verified, refused to execute K25 scope (would have clobbered K26-K34a ships per K34 cli scope-disagreement-by-on-disk-classification), surfaced via reply, operator re-uploaded correct K35 prompt. **K37 lessons logged:**

(clxv) **K20 sandbox-clone-block extends to ALL existing-file modifications on mounted Windows folders — folder-ACL-dependent, not blanket-mount.** K20 originally locked the pattern at `git clone`-into-mount; K37 surfaces a finer-grained pattern: vmwp.exe block applies to ANY sandbox-side rm OR overwrite of an EXISTING file on the mounted `efilist-argument-library/` folder. NEW-file creates work fine (Cowork created 7 files in efilist-argument-library/ this session without issue). Mount-write-permission varies by per-folder ACL: `wuld-ink/` (operator project) accepts existing-file writes (proven via 12-file Python pass on src/ HTML); `efilist-argument-library/` (sibling project under same Projects/ parent) blocks them. Both mounts show `drwx------` permission flag in sandbox listing; the actual block must be Windows-side NTFS ACL or Cowork-side per-folder allowlist. Mitigation when block hits: queue all rm + overwrite operations to operator-side PowerShell handoff; sandbox can stage NEW files to `/outputs/` scratchpad for operator-cp into repo. Pattern reach: this is the standing constraint for ALL cross-repo work to projects other than wuld-ink. K38+ investigation cost: ~1 bash call comparing mount listings + per-folder write permission test. Continues K20 file-system-write-block discipline family.

(clxvi) **Handout/manifest PRESERVE assertions can be wrong against actual on-disk repo state — md5-verify before trusting publish-without-action plan.** K37 handout's `VERIFY-AND-PRESERVE` block claimed `combined.html` + `rebuttal_grading_ledger.json` were already at v3.7.3 byte-identical state in repo; pre-flight md5 audit found both had v3.7.2-era md5s (combined.html `2accf16a` vs expected `29f9d5c0`; ledger `a85c1191` vs expected `9b0b291f`). Likely cause: handout authored from canon `archive_attestation.harness_green_attestation_v3_7_3.combined_coherence_note` (which described the pre-sync state where combined.html "carried at v3.7.2 md5 with explicit coherence-note flag; resync deferred"), without re-deriving against actual repo bytes at handout-authoring time. Lock: when handout/manifest claims a file is "already at target state, no action," pre-flight md5 verify against canon's expected target md5 BEFORE committing to skip the file. Cost: ~1 bash call (`md5sum file1 file2 ...`); catches false-preserve cases that would have committed mixed-version artifact sets (corpus + jsx + index at v3.7.3 but combined.html + ledger lingering at v3.7.2 — which would silently break the integrity-contract claim in README). Particularly relevant to PATCH-class publications where most files genuinely DON'T change and PRESERVE-without-action is the default expectation; the exception case is where the SHIPPED single-file (combined.html) needs the same content advance as the spine. Refines K20 lesson `md5-locked artifact contract`: contracts are AUTHORITATIVE only when md5-verified against actual repo files; manifest text alone is not enough.

(clxvii) **Cross-repo dual-PowerShell handoff is the new K-session shape for library publication rounds.** K20 had single-repo (library only) operator-side publish via `publish-library-v3-7.ps1` 9-step script; K37 introduces wuld.ink-side coupled refresh (12 HTML files referencing v3.7.x version strings + md5 + byte count). Maintain commit-message symmetry: library commit references the canonical version bump + canon-attestation; wuld.ink commit references the cross-repo link refresh + provenance pointer to library commit SHA.

**K37a lessons logged:**

(clxviii) **Sandbox `.git/index.lock` contention persists into operator PowerShell session as silent-failure source.** K37 sandbox session left `.git/index.lock` on the mounted library repo (sandbox couldn't unlink it per K37 clxv). When operator then ran PowerShell `git commit` + `git tag` in the same repo, both failed with `Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists` — but operator's PowerShell display scrolled past the errors and the next `git push origin v3.7.3` succeeded against the stale local tag pointer. Lock pattern: any cross-repo session involving sandbox-side file operations on a mounted Windows repo MUST prepend the operator-side PowerShell with defensive lock cleanup: `Remove-Item -Force .git\index.lock; Remove-Item -Force .git\objects\maintenance.lock; Get-ChildItem .git -Filter "*.lock" -Recurse | ForEach-Object { Remove-Item -Force $_.FullName }`. Cost: ~5 lines of PowerShell; catches the silent-failure root cause. Continues K20 + K37 clxv file-system-write-block discipline family.

(clxix) **PowerShell smoke against `*.html` URLs must use `curl.exe -L` (follow-redirects) when target site has `.html` extension-strip enabled.** Cloudflare Pages auto-308-redirects `*.html` URLs to extension-stripped paths (e.g., `combined.html` → `/combined`). PowerShell `curl.exe -s -o file URL` writes the 308 redirect's empty body, not the destination body. Diagnostic fingerprint: 0-byte file + md5 `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e` (the empty-string md5) is unambiguous evidence the curl didn't follow a redirect. Lock pattern: PowerShell smoke for any Pages-deployed `.html` resource MUST use `curl.exe -sL ...` to follow OR test the extension-stripped path directly (e.g., `/combined` not `/combined.html`). Reachability via `curl.exe -sIL URL | Select-String "^HTTP/"` surfaces BOTH the 308 AND the followed 200 — better diagnostic than single-status check. If a smoke EVER returns `d41d8cd9...` for a non-empty resource, the URL is redirecting and curl didn't follow. Refines K20 + K37 cxv smoke discipline.

(clxx) **Library-Claude's class-label discipline (STANDING for wuld.ink-side cross-repo work).** Per library-Claude's K37a consult: invariants subtree bytes unchanged → PATCH-class, regardless of how much canon attestation paperwork moved (v3.7.1's attestation-only change is PATCH, NOT "MINOR-bookkeeping"). For wuld.ink Cowork when describing library versions in `/library-about/` or `/argument-library/` pages: default to canon's PATCH/MINOR/MAJOR classification per invariants-subtree-bytes (not commit-message volume). Cross-link to wuld.ink-side citation discipline: integrity contracts (md5 + byte count) propagate from canon's `release_artifact_md5_set_per_release_manifest_*` blocks; version semantics propagate from invariants-subtree-anchor stability.

(clxxi) **Library-Claude's handout md5-default-REPLACE rule (STANDING for cross-repo K38+ sessions).** A file goes in PRESERVE only when canon's attested md5 for that file is known to match the current REPO state. If canon attests a sync that postdates the last repo push, the file goes in REPLACE (or at minimum VERIFY-FIRST with replace-on-mismatch as the DEFAULT branch, not the fallback). Cowork-side check at handout-receipt: `git log -1 --format=%cI <repo_file>` on each PRESERVE candidate vs canon's `last_updated` on the corresponding attestation block. If canon's timestamp postdates the repo file's last commit timestamp, REPLACE. K37 lesson clxvi locked the pre-flight md5-verify; clxxi adds the WHY — handout authors operating from canon attestations don't necessarily know the repo's last-push state. Continues K37 clxvi + K34 cli scope-disagreement-via-on-disk-classification family.

### K280 (2026-09-05, FILM-BAND FIX — YouTube Error 153 (my regression) + the play glyph sitting on the title card; NO PIN, one file, site-only): Track (Josiah eyeballed the K279 band on desktop and phone: the embed returned **"Video player configuration error — Error 153"** and the ▶ overlaid the word "IS" on the cover art. Both mine.)

- **K279 LANDED — GREEN.** Commit `aa2f814`; served essay page carries `wuld:film` with **zero iframes**, cover byte-exact `10adfd46`, apparatus carries `EAvxK0f3oRo`, `/releases.json` `93d2e054`, changelog chip label shipped.
- **ROOT CAUSE (ccxliii, and the lesson is the old one): I deviated from a known-working house recipe for no reason.** K279's facade set `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` on the constructed iframe, reasoning "maximum privacy". **YouTube authorises an embed by its referrer**; with no referrer it cannot resolve the embedding origin and the player fails closed with **Error 153**. The site already had a proven recipe at `/watch/` (K220, live and working) and it uses `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` — which still sends only the origin, so nothing was gained by deviating and the player broke.
- **DIAGNOSIS WAS CHEAP AND SHOULD BE THE DEFAULT:** `https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=<url>&format=json` returned **200 with full metadata and an embeddable iframe**, proving the video is public-enough and embedding is NOT disabled in Studio — which isolated the fault to our own markup in one call instead of sending Josiah to hunt through YouTube settings. **Use oEmbed before ever blaming an upload's configuration.**
- **FIX 1 — the iframe now matches `/watch/` VERBATIM:** `?autoplay=1&rel=0&modestbranding=1&playsinline=1` (`playsinline` was also missing — iOS would have gone fullscreen on tap), `allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"`, `allowfullscreen`, `referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"`. **The click-to-load posture is untouched** — still zero iframes in the static HTML, still nothing fetched from youtube-nocookie until a deliberate click. Privacy was never in the referrer policy; it is in the deferral.
- **FIX 2 — the play glyph moves out of the artwork.** It was `position:absolute; inset:0` centred, which put ▶ squarely on the "IS" of a designed title card (visible on both desktop and phone). It is now inline at the head of the bottom label bar in accent colour: `▶ Play here — nothing loads from YouTube until you click`. The affordance and its explanation are one object, and the cover art is unobstructed.
- **GATES:** `no-referrer` occurrences 0 · `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` 1 · `playsinline=1` 1 · static `<iframe` 0 · absolute-positioned `.film-play` 0 · page parses with zero unclosed tags, U+FFFD 0 · diff `5+/6-`, one file.

### K287 (2026-09-06, THE LAST OF THE MOBILE WORK — `/void-engine/` full reflow + the ambient bar's real defect; `?v` mobile-a11y/ambient-player K275→K287; 75 files; NO PIN, DESKTOP GEOMETRY-INERT): Track (the K286 handoff prompt, executed as written except for two corrections the measurements forced — both recorded below, both load-bearing for whoever reads this next.)

- **K286 LANDED — GREEN.** Commit `8a88598`; HEAD==origin, clean tree. The K286 carry line "K286 landing: pending" is closed by this session.
- **CORRECTION 1, AND IT REFRAMES THE WHOLE VOID-ENGINE ITEM. The 388 residual "sub-44 touch targets" were 370 buttons that are invisible on a phone.** `.nadd` — the per-card NEG control, one per lexicon entry, 397 of them — is `opacity:0` until `.card:hover`. A touch device cannot hover, so on a phone the negation set was never a small target: it was **unreachable**. Sizing those 370 without revealing them would have shipped 370 invisible 44px tap zones inside the cards, which is worse than the bug. The fix reveals them at `@media (hover: none)` and then gives the 44px box; the negative block margin spends the card's own 18px padding instead of growing `.cfoot`, so **the 397-card list did not get taller — measured document height at 390 FELL, 103,002 → 102,852.** K275's counter was right about the number and wrong about what it was counting.
- **CORRECTION 2: the ambient bar was never a horizontal-scroll source.** Both the K275 stratum and the K287 kickoff call it "the last remaining horizontal-scroll source site-wide". Measured on a purpose-built isolation harness with no `html{overflow-x:hidden}` mask: **the document never scrolled horizontally at any width, before or after** — `.ambient-player` is `position:fixed`, and a fixed element's overflow does not extend document scroll width. The real defect is quieter and worse. The bar composes to ~1088px minimum (eleven `flex-shrink:0` children, one shrinkable track, plus the two chips `wrong-hour.js` docks at runtime — hence "intermittent and JS-state-dependent"), and it had **no `overflow` rule at all**, so from 641px to 1088px the track name collapsed to **zero width** and the right-hand controls — including `[v]`, the bar's only escape hatch — rendered past the right edge with no way to reach them. Live bite: tablets, split screens, half-width desktop windows. Fixed with three declarations that remove nothing: `overflow-x:auto` (+ suppressed scrollbar) so the strip scrolls itself, and `min-width:7rem` on `.ambient-track` so the name survives. Corollary found on the way: **the `@media (max-width: 480px)` block in `ambient-player.css` is dead code** — 480 sits inside the ≤640 hide K275 added. Left in place, commented, as the composition to restore if the bar ever returns to phones.
- **THE OTHER OVERFLOW WAS THE STICKY TAB STRIP, and it was clipping, not scrolling.** `#engine-toggle`'s three tabs measure 406px in a 390px strip; `html{overflow-x:hidden}` clipped it, so **"Transmission" was unreachable**, and the labels wrapped to two lines for a **90px sticky header on every scroll of a 103,000px page**. Equalised the tabs (`flex:1 1 0`) and tightened the strip's own padding/tracking: **406→390, 90px→45px, one line, all three reachable.**
- **WHERE THE RULES HAD TO GO, AND WHY NOT THE PAGE.** `src/void-engine/index.html`'s inline `<style>` (lines 47–639) is **not chrome** — it is one of the two regions wholesale-substituted from the void-engine-suite's `DUAL_ENGINE` source on every engine sync. Anything patched there dies at the next paste-relay. So every rule lives in `mobile-a11y.css`, which loads **before** that inline block — meaning equal-specificity rules **lose** (hazard ccl). Every selector therefore carries a real ancestor or tag qualifier (`.cfoot .nadd`, `body #engine-toggle button`, `label.tl`). No `!important`; no `html.mnav-on` either, because that class is JS-set and these rules must hold without JS.
- **MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED, ON THE SHIPPED BYTES.** Repo files served from a local mirror (the K284 recipe) and rendered in the container's chromium, all three engine panes, clip-aware overflow (a rect past the viewport inside an `overflow:hidden` ancestor is not an offender — the un-patched counter false-positives on the Transmission pane's animated `.ghost-word`). **Sub-44: void 389→5, signal 6→3, transmission 3→3. Uncontained horizontal overflow: 0 at 320 / 360 / 390 / 430, every pane.** Residual is three named classes, all deliberate: 2× `.tcb` (22×22, wrapped by a 44px `label.tl` — a 44px checkbox is a different design, not an accessible one) · 2× `.page-footer a` (site chrome, `footer.css`, would need its own `?v` bump) · 1× `.mnav-home` (68×40; growing it moves the sticky bar K282/K283 tuned to 71px on all 70 pages — deliberately untouched).

- **THREE PREMISES CORRECTED BEFORE BUILDING, all by reading the engine, and all change what the tool measures.** (1) *"A single weight-9 pattern does NOT clear `MISS_THRESHOLD = 16`… PROVE how the floor fires."* The floor does not fire through scoring at all: **stage 1 of `match()` scans only crisis entries, any hit with score > 0 wins, before the oracle lane, before the repeat lane, exempt from dampening, with no threshold.** And scores are `BASE[mode] + weight` — a **MAX** over matching patterns, never a sum — so a `contains` w9 form scores **69**, a `tokens_any` w9 scores 24; the premise took the weight for the score. (2) *"Threshold headroom — an entry reachable only by an exact 15-form pile-up."* Impossible on this engine: nothing piles, and the **smallest possible match score on this corpus is 24** (responses 62, since only the floor uses `tokens_any`), so `MISS_THRESHOLD` never bites. Replaced by a reachability profile. (3) The **K253 stratum's** "Latin greet on a third consecutive hello" is wrong: three consecutive hellos give `mg-greet-01 → mg-repeat-01 → mg-deflect-01` (the repeat lane intercepts the second, `prior ≥ 2` misses the third), and **no schedule of three `hello`s can reach `mg-greet-04`** — proven exhaustively over every pair of gaps 1..12; the repeat window (5) and the dampening window (8) never align. It is reachable via `hi` spaced five turns apart (`greet-01` → `greet-04`) and via its own forms `welcome` / `salve` / `good day`.

- **Standing hazards:** carry K213-K297 unchanged, plus **cclxxi — a local-mirror crawl of this site is contaminated by the site's own service worker.** The pages register it under `pointer: coarse`, it claims the origin after the first navigations, and it then serves `?v` assets cache-first from its cache, so a mobile crawl measures stale CSS and the answer depends on how many pages were crawled. Set `serviceWorkers: 'block'` on any crawling context, assert the measured document's own `location.pathname` against the route requested (that assert caught a heading being reported on a page that has none — a `meta refresh` stub), and **calibrate every new instrument against an answer already known from another instrument before believing a single number it produces.** A harness that disagrees with a direct probe is the harness's bug until proven otherwise.

Scope the assertion to where the string is load-bearing (`-- src`), and expect any prose file describing a version bump to contain both versions forever after. The tree was left correct but uncommitted (37 modified, 6 untracked, 0 staged, HEAD unmoved), so recovery was a **resume** block — result-guards in place of base-guards, no re-move, no re-sweep (the sweep is idempotent and its own internal gate was always correct, since it walks only the `src` root it is handed). **Second-order lesson, the one that generalises: a gate placed AFTER an irreversible mutation must be evaluated against the POST-mutation tree, not only the pre-mutation one.** Every gate before the first `Move-Item` had been dry-run this session; the ones after it had not, because there was no post-mutation tree to run them against until the operator made one. Build that tree in the harness and run the tail of the block against it before handing it over.

Present→past has no inverse in the map, so each pass strictly reduces the unshifted verbs remaining and termination is guaranteed. The multi-verb count is the convergence driver and decays 14 → 7 → 0. **Separately, the historical growth (165 → 102 → 87) was NOT this at all** — K305's own header records that the K299 map was unrecoverable and this one was rebuilt WIDER. - **AND MY TEST'S PREMISE IS BROKEN BY THEIR CROP — my error, not another candidate.** *"Picture-fraction invariant ⇒ geometry settles it"* holds only under **pure scaling**. v10 does `scale → crop`, and the crop removes **46 rows carrying the breadcrumb strip and the footer — text rows, above-average in qualifying pixels.** Both terms move: the numerator drops by the qualifying pixels in those rows, the denominator by 46 rows of area. **Invariance is no longer the null hypothesis**, and the test as written would read a legitimate crop effect as an imaging change.

rounding. The element sits 1.3% down the document, where little above it has wrapped;
deeper positions accumulate more added height, so the local ratio RISES with depth --
1.2984 near the top, 1.3102 overall. Exactly that pattern. The factor varies with
position, which is a long way of saying it is not a factor. 1.25 is wrong; 1.00 is
also wrong for combined.html.

CCCIII. A scroll literal is a DERIVED quantity, not a parameter. A take that scrolls
to reveal a specific element must compute the scroll from that element's measured
position at the geometry it is shot at. Carrying a number authored at another
geometry is an unmeasured claim about reflow, whether multiplied by 1.25 or by 1.

CCCIV. The load-bearing check covers regions; regions come from selectors.
tk.scroll(N) declares no selector, therefore no region, therefore nothing to contain.
A take that scrolls past its payoff and holds on blank space reports 0 outside frame,
0 behind bezel -- the instrument was never given anything to look at. "107 regions
across 17 takes, one finding" is a true statement about the regions the instrument
has, read as coverage of the takes. Fix in their idiom: tk.scroll_to(selector, sec),
which derives the scroll AND registers the element as load-bearing, closing ccciii
and ccciv together and covering scroll takes with the containment check already
built. Literal scrolls become the exception that must be justified.

MULTIPLIER IS THE WRONG SHAPE OF OBJECT. Since scrollBy / scrollTo / scrollY and
getBoundingClientRect are all OUTER, headroom is a single-space subtraction, and reproducing a take
authored at zoom 1 with literal N at zoom Z is exact and AFFINE:
    same DEVICE headroom     M = N     + ( outerDocY_Z(E) -     outerDocY_1(E) )     pure offset
    same CONTENT fraction    M = Z.N   + ( outerDocY_Z(E) - Z . outerDocY_1(E) )     affine
Against this seat's h2 (outerDocY 644 -> 807, Z 1.25, N 560):
    proportional   M = 700 + (807 - 805) = 702      matches measured 702
    literal-84     M = 560 + (807 - 644) = 723      matches measured 723
Both measured numbers, exactly, from one formula. The offset term is the element's own reflow
displacement in outer space: per-page, per-depth, uncarryable by any scalar. It also explains why 1.25
looked like a rule -- on wuld.ink/argument-library/ that term is +2 px, so 1.25 was 0.3% wrong there,
not 20%. On combined.html the same term is 644 - 620 = +24 px, twelve times larger. scroll_to makes

## K311a — cccvii (do not accumulate); the rate withdrawn; absolute positioning also removes scroll anchoring

CCCVII. DO NOT ACCUMULATE — SET THE POSITION, NEVER ADD TO IT. Relative stepping (scrollBy with a
per-frame delta) applies each delta to the ALREADY-SNAPPED current position, so every step's snapping
error feeds the next step's starting point. The compounded result is deterministic, non-monotonic in
distance AND in step count, and it CHANGES SIGN. Measured this seat, wuld.ink/argument-library/,
zoom 1.25, ease-in-out quad, one step per rAF, three identical runs per cell:
    723.0 @  60 steps   701.6   -21.4   -2.96%
    723.0 @  30 steps   725.8   + 2.8   +0.39%
    723.0 @ 120 steps   725.8   + 2.8   +0.39%
    180.2 @  60 steps   180.6   + 0.4   +0.22%
    400.5 @  60 steps   400.0   - 0.5   -0.12%
Absolute positioning per frame: EIGHTEEN configurations (3 distances x 3 step counts x 3 roundings,
including no rounding at all) landed identically -- 723.4 and 179.8, the +-0.4 being the 0.8 px device
grid at Z 1.25. Rounding is not what fixes it; not accumulating is. Same move as note_region taking its
box and scroll_to resolving at shoot geometry: remove the channel rather than police it.

THE RATE WITHDRAWN (theirs, K311f). "2.3% short in every take" was one cell -- 180.2 at 60 steps on
combined.html -- generalised to every scroll, inside the relay reporting the read-back discipline that
exists to prevent exactly that. Their own table now shows +2.11 / -2.33 / -2.33 at 180.2 and
-0.14 / +0.14 / +0.69 at 723, confirming sign-variance and non-monotonicity on their page too. Their
stated mechanism (truncation accumulating across the loop) is refuted by 120 steps landing no worse
than 60, on both seats' data.

ROUNDING IS PAGE-DEPENDENT. Cumulative-rounded deltas were exact within the device grid on
combined.html at all nine cells and SHORT on wuld.ink/argument-library/ at two of three distances.
Not a contradiction -- the finding: rounded deltas work only where the rounding grid and the page's own
snap grid agree, so a fix whose correctness depends on which page it points at is a coincidence, not a
fix. Absolute positioning removes the dependence.

OPEN, AND FLAGGED TO THEM BEFORE THE BATCH FINISHES. scrollTo every frame does not only stop error
feeding forward; it also OVERRIDES Chrome's scroll anchoring. Their own K311d measured that anchoring
at T14 asked 180 / moved 202, and T17 asked 201 / moved 214 -- read as benign under the old harness,
where anchoring absorbed content settling above the viewport and the PICTURE stayed put while scrollY
diverged. Under absolute positioning that compensation is discarded: T14's landing moves ~22 px and
T17's ~13 px, and whatever anchoring was absorbing now shows as motion. Their §3b documented it and
their §2 removed it with nothing connecting the two. Test is one run on their side (shoot T14 on both
harnesses, compare final scrollY, diff the frames). If the picture moves, the shape is SETTLE FIRST,
THEN POSITION ABSOLUTELY -- not a choice between a harness that drifts and one that overrides.
Recommended holding the 17-take batch until T14 answers, since it costs one run now and seventeen later.

WHY THESE FAILED AND THE PICTURE CLAIMS DID NOT. Three vacuous/scope failures in this thread -- the
flash gate that could not fail, the guard nearly verified against a fault injection that does nothing
(overflow:hidden does not block programmatic scrolling in Chrome), and the 2.3% rate. All three were
claims about the INSTRUMENT, and the instrument had no independent referent. The world-facing claims
(does the bloom show, does the dissolve land, does T17 hold on nothing) were checkable against frames
and got caught fast. An instrument claim needs a referent that is not another instrument claim;
re-running the measurement is the cheapest one available.

quantity, not a travel quantity. Still to be confirmed against a real capture from the absolute harness.

## K311b — cccix, cccx; cccviii as rule and design; the 867 withdrawn; and my area veto was ranked backwards

CCCIX (video seat's text, allocated here). WHEN ONE PIPELINE'S OUTPUT IS ANOTHER PIPELINE'S INPUT, a
change to the first invalidates the second's work in flight -- and neither pipeline can see it. The
capture harness does not know it is being watched; the room render does not know its subject is moving.
Any asset that crosses between them carries the version of the thing that produced it, and a re-render
is scheduled by that version rather than by whether the render "looks right".
DEMONSTRATED: T04_three_depths (the take baked onto the room monitor) ends on tk.scroll(700, 11.0) --
precisely the operation whose landing moves between the old harness and absolute positioning. Four room
shots were rendering a superseded monitor. Killed at roomA_open 276/276 complete-stale, roomC_breath
156/156 complete-stale, roomE_pov_push 120/120 complete-stale, roomD_tail 87/336 partial, roomB_title
0/306 unstarted -- ~550 frames saved. Closed mechanically, not by memory: screenfeed_seq/source.json is
written at extraction with the source's md5, byte count and frame count, and every shot manifest carries
it (screen_source_T04.mp4 / e7c986a875a9320152ec22f16906423f / 6,615,420 B / 2021 frames). A NAMED file
established nothing -- T04_three_depths.mp4 is the same name before and after the re-shoot. Third
instance of ONE rule, not three rules: the marker carrying its md5 instead of a version name,
note_region taking its box instead of fetching one, the capture carrying its hash instead of a filename.
REMOVE THE CHANNEL THAT LETS TWO HALVES DISAGREE SILENTLY.

CCCVIII -- AS RULE AND DESIGN ONLY. Deliberately committed WITHOUT its constants: AREA_FLOOR,
BASE_BRIGHT, the density cut and the band names all moved at least once inside one day, two of them
because this seat pushed on them. Committing a number still in flight is what started the preceding
four relays.
    RULE: keyframing a value does not make it visible. A treatment's effect is established by the
    treatment being visible in the OUTPUT, never by the parameter being set, and never by the render
    completing without error. Render the frame twice -- with and without -- and diff. The referent is
    the difference between two pictures, which is the one thing in this class that is not an opinion.
    DESIGN: baseline once per shot then one render per treatment (1+N, not 2N); report AMPLITUDE and
    AREA separately, because neither alone is sufficient; on INERT, re-render EXAGGERATED to separate a
    dead switch from a live switch with a setting or framing that hides it; each treatment DECLARES the
    frame at which its own effect is maximal, "static" being a declaration and not a default, since a
    sweep that guesses the probe frame can only ever report a LOWER BOUND on activity.
FOUND BY IT, three-for-three before it existed: the bloom (threshold 175 on pages of median luma 15),
the room monitor, the Yurei apparition keyframed on a subject camC_rake does not have in frame. Found
BY it after: chin_grills INERT in all three shots at max exactly 1/255 -- nothing lights that face, so
no reflective treatment on it can read at any size, which is the generalisation the wordmark should
have forced.
DEFECTS FOUND IN THE SWEEP BY THE SWEEP, all theirs, all reported unprompted: (a) INERT set at
max < 0.002 against an 8-bit floor of 1/255 = 0.00392 -- arithmetically unreachable, the flash gate
reproduced inside the instrument built to catch that class, on its first run; (b) the probe frame was
null for the treatment it tested, an apparition envelope at its plateau being identical to no envelope;
(c) DETAIL["desk_wear"] checked by the caller and not by the function, so the sweep read a dead SWITCH
as a dead TREATMENT; (d) base_luma_on_changed computed from the frame WITH the treatment rather than
without -- named for what was wanted, read from the wrong array, plausible enough to ship. A name is a
claim; that is the marker lesson at variable scope.

MINE, THIS ROUND. I gave them two corrections and ranked them backwards: area_1q as required and the
8x8 density split as OPTIONAL. Wrong order. area_1q alone vetoed the chin LEDs as "negligible" -- 41 px
of 2,073,600, forty times under the floor, and the most legible thing on the chin in every render
anyone has looked at. The opposite error to the bloom's, produced by the fix for the bloom, and caught
only by the axis I had called optional. THE TWO ARE A PAIR, NOT A PRIMARY AND AN EXTRA: amplitude
without area misses the bloom, area without shape suppresses the LEDs. The area_1q reasoning itself
stands -- this footage sits at mean luma 0.05-0.09, where a treatment lifting half the frame by 2/255
gives max 0.0078 and area_4q exactly 0, vetoed as absent before it can reach the faint band, which is
how a grade or an ambient fill fails and exactly what a viewer would see.

CCCX. WHEN AN INSTRUMENT IS FOUND BROKEN, ENUMERATE EVERY CLAIM IT PRODUCED BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE.
Finding the break does not retract its history; the fix feels like the resolution and is not one.
Demonstrated twice in one session, and BOTH TIMES it took the other seat asking -- neither of us ran it
unprompted on our own instrument. Their file-size heuristic, enumerated:
    screenfeed_full: 867 of 1400 frames black          WRONG -- measured properly, ZERO
    screenfeed_full: content only in frames 14-245     WRONG -- same threshold, same error
    first T04 extraction: 1400 frames, zero dark       right, BY LUCK; since confirmed by luma
    second T04 extraction: 1301 of 2021 dark           WRONG -- caught at the time
    look-dev "busiest frame" pick (sf_00203)           harmless; picked densest, not brightest
Four claims, three wrong. The 867 is WITHDRAWN from the relay record and from the project document:
screenfeed_full first 1400 frames, YAVG via signalstats, min 16.02 / p50 25.94 / max 28.06, frames
under YAVG 10 = 0. Not one frame is black. THE DECISION SURVIVES ON THE OTHER GROUND: a monitor inside
the room showing the film that contains the room is a RECURSION, which has nothing to do with luma and

CRANE. roomF_crane's locked tail landed inside a hold BY ACCIDENT -- settled at frame 163, tail
163-240, hold at 153-288, with nothing in either file that would have caught a different offset. Now

STANDING. T01b: 723, place = 0.09621, centre-anchored, innerHeight 1080 -- a framing quantity, not a
travel quantity, and still owed a confirmation against a real capture from the absolute harness rather
than from a browser pane. T01: left +158, top +194 inside SAFE. Hazard allocation is now assigned by

## K311c — stops replace the ratio; "in range" is not "same content"; P5's spec arrives and its safety section is inverted

CCCVIII, THIRD AXIS (still no constants committed). The contrast axis they added was SIGNED and would
have suppressed every darkening treatment -- a vignette halving reads 0.5 where the LEDs read 4.4, so
any floor above 1.0 vetoes all darkening and any floor below compresses it into noise. The vignette is
already in this film's chain, so it was queued rather than hypothetical. Fixed on this seat's proposal
by measuring in STOPS, |log2(new/old)|, which is direction-blind:
    chin LEDs      0.145 -> 0.78     2.43 stops
    vignette       0.5x              1.00 stops
    bloom on pixels already at the top          0.08 stops
A floor near half a stop passes the first two and rejects the third. Their earlier absolute-brightness
version was worse than one-directional -- it compared display-referred PNG values (AgX lifts darks
hard; the chin reads 0.145 in a frame of mean 0.05-0.09) against a threshold picked as if the values
were scene-referred, and vetoed the LEDs for sitting on nearly-black ground.
THE AXES OR TOWARD VISIBLE, NEVER AND. keycap_legends at 0.06 stops and desk_grime at 0.01 read
"visible" on area alone, which is correct and which will look wrong to whoever next reads a report full
of results they cannot see. The rule that stops the tightening: A FALSE "VISIBLE" COSTS A GLANCE; A
FALSE "INERT" SHIPS. Recorded here so it is not optimised away later.

SELF-TEST BEATS SELF-CHECK (theirs, better than this seat's proposal). I proposed injecting one
unwired flag, confirming the "switch not wired" band fires, and removing it. They made it permanent:
__selftest_unwired, a flag no code reads, swept every run and REQUIRED to come back INERT; if it fails,
the run says so and every INERT in it is suspect. Mine proves the band worked on the day I checked;
theirs proves it worked on the run whose results are being read. Conceded.

"OUT-POINTS INSIDE SOURCE" IS A CLAIM ABOUT BOUNDS, NOT CONTENT. The _center boundary-nudge fix moved
three of seventeen takes -- T07 -168, T08 +42, T17 +90, net -36 frames. T07 is in neither cut so its
2.9 s is free. T08 and T17 are in both cuts and GREW, and they signed "no cut timing moved" on
out-points sitting inside source length. That proves the cut does not run off the end; it does NOT
prove the cut frames the same material. If T08's 42 frames arrived anywhere before frame 722 then
everything after slid and src 102-722 now shows different content at the same numbers. OPEN, and it is
a two-frame diff per take against batches they already hold, not a shoot. Same shape as the rest of
this thread with a different noun.
ANSWERED IN PART (K311n) AND THE ANSWER OVERSHOOTS. They settled T08 from its own MARKS rather than a
frame diff -- click #vbtn-map at f102 (the window's IN exactly) and the next click at f683 (39 frames
before the OUT), both unmoved in the new 1741-frame take. Better evidence than the diff, and it proves
the insertion is AFTER f683. It does NOT prove "after 722", which is what they wrote: 39 frames of the
window sit past the last anchor, and the take grew by 42. Forty-two frames of growth against a

than to relax. AN ANCHOR PROVES WHAT PRECEDES IT, NOT WHAT FOLLOWS.
T17 does not clear and cannot be made to: it records no marks, and its content changed by design when
the exists/declare_absent restructure replaced the bare except that held five seconds on nothing. They

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THAT DOCUMENT, in the section it tells the reader to read first:
1. ITS AMPLITUDE ADVICE IS INVERTED. It says a 10%-of-peak-white swing is "a very small number in
   absolute terms" on a dark palette. Relative luminance is normalised with 1.0 = peak white -- the
   correction they handed this seat in K310c, applied to their own paragraph -- and gamma compresses
   the dark end: from a #0E0E10 ground (L ~ 0.004) a legal 0.10 swing reaches sRGB ~#5B5B5B, near-black
   to mid-grey. A DARK PAGE HAS MORE PERCEPTUAL ROOM UNDER THE CRITERION THAN A LIGHT ONE, not less.
2. TWO OF THE FOUR FLASH GATES ARE AUTOMATIC HERE, NOT ONE. They correctly note a page-wide effect
   satisfies the 25% AREA condition by construction. The criterion also requires the darker state below
   relative luminance 0.80, which every state on this palette is. Only amplitude and rate remain.
3. ITS §10 GATES THE MASCOT'S FADE ON prefers-reduced-motion. Wrong switch: that preference targets
   vestibular triggers (parallax, zoom, translation), and a slow cross-fade is what the guidance
   recommends SUBSTITUTING for motion. Gating opacity on it makes first paint a static bezel, less
   alive than the film Josiah asked to adopt. The line falls between vestibular and opacity.
Also flagged, not a safety item: a live filter firing loading/loaded per keystroke drives the LEDs at
4-6 Hz and every transition is "required by the state," which is exactly the justification their rule
accepts. Debounce the LED to the state's MEANING, not to the event.
